scenes.narration: Certifications brings together the types your department tracks and the records held by people or units. In this fictional Chicago Fire department, the dashboard starts with one record pending verification. Boden can inspect his own pending record, but this page offers no Verify button. Record holders cannot verify their own records. We will create a clearly marked software exercise for another member, then use the normal administrative review path. Use the viewing, management, and setup permissions your department has assigned.

scenes.narration: Settings separates role enforcement from expiry notifications. The saved mode is Off, with thirty days of grace and pending records not treated as valid for role requirements. Warn only permits role changes with warnings; Enforce can block unqualified role additions and remove members after grace. We inspect these choices, restore Off, and leave Save untouched. Off does not disable expiry processing or notifications. The holder and administrator-digest options remain checked, with lead days of sixty, thirty, fourteen, seven, and one. These settings do not prove message delivery.

scenes.narration: Chicago Fire can use this pattern to organize a clearly identified exercise record. Community care and mental health teams can track operational training without patient detail. Search and rescue can distinguish person records from equipment records; security teams can organize reviewed staff records; wildland teams can keep seasonal training references current; and industrial response teams can separate staff records from unit inspections. In every setting, define the type, enter deliberate dates, use an authorized reviewer, and verify saved status. A software label alone does not authorize real duties.
